# Release test plan

Every pysacd release runs this plan in full, on the release commit or on the published files, and
records each result in the release issue with the [sign-off table](#sign-off). CI proves what the
tests say; this plan covers what CI can't see: real discs, the published wheels, other platforms,
longer fuzzing, speed and memory. The plan was validated on 2026-11-23 against 0.5.5 (the
published-file steps), against master after 0.5.5 as the next release would run it (the pre-tag
steps on generated discs), and on 0.5.5's own release run (real discs and timings); each section
says which.

## How to use this plan

- **Two words stand for versions.** VERSION is the release under test (`version` in
  `pyproject.toml` after the bump) and PREVIOUS is the release before it (`git describe --tags
  --abbrev=0` on master before tagging, without the `v`). Every other value is literal.
- **When each step runs.** CI and the Linux runs of step 1, and steps 2 to 5 and 8, run on the
  release commit before the version bump (pysacd writes its version into its output, so two trees
  compare only at the same version). The other platforms of step 1, and steps 6, 7 and 9, run on
  the published files after the tag. A step that fails blocks the tag; a
  failure after the tag means a patch release.
- **What blocks.** Any difference in output that isn't documented, any sanitizer report, crash or
  leak, a Quick start or docs command that fails as written, a slowdown over the
  [threshold](#8-performance), or a security finding without a `go`.
- **Where.** Linux steps run in a Fedora 44 container, like CI. Heavy steps (real discs, fuzzing,
  timings) run on lab machines named here by CPU only; timings hold the machine's benchmark lock.
  Run every test suite under a memory cap (`PYSACD_TEST_MEMORY_MB=4096`, or the container's
  `--memory`), with `TMPDIR` on a disk.

## 1. The suite on every platform

**What CI covers** on the release pull request (link its run in the sign-off):

| Job | Platform | Python | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lint + tests` | Fedora 44 x86-64 container | 3.10 to 3.15 | ruff, mypy, the suite with FLAC, only the expected skips, a 4 GiB memory cap |
| `tests under ASan + UBSan` | Fedora 44 x86-64 | 3.13 | the suite with the engine and fuzz harnesses instrumented |
| `tests under TSan` | Ubuntu runner | 3.13 | the suite with the engine's threads under ThreadSanitizer |
| `engine leak check` | Fedora 44 x86-64 | 3.13 | LeakSanitizer on every seed, valgrind memcheck on eight |
| `compare with sacd_extract` | Fedora 44 x86-64 | 3.13 | generated discs against `sacd_extract` from the pinned commit |
| `portability` | macOS (arm64), Windows x86-64 | 3.13 | the engine with warnings as errors, then the suite |
| `wheels (release)` | manylinux x86-64 and aarch64, musllinux x86-64, macOS arm64 and x86-64, Windows x86-64 | 3.13 | each wheel built, its CET mark (x86-64 manylinux), libFLAC and `minos` checked, `tests/wheel_smoke.py` in a clean environment |

**By hand, on the published wheels** (after the tag), because CI never runs the suite there:

| Platform | Where | What to run |
|---|---|---|
| macOS 15, arm64 | macOS 15 in a VM on Apple hardware, no developer tools | the [Quick start](#6-quick-start-in-a-fresh-container) with `pip install pysacd==VERSION`, then `tests/wheel_smoke.py` from the tag |
| Windows 11, x86-64 | a Windows 11 VM | `pip install pysacd==VERSION`, then `tests/wheel_smoke.py` from the tag |
| Linux aarch64 | a Fedora 44 aarch64 container (`podman run --arch arm64`, emulated on an x86-64 lab machine, or native when an aarch64 machine is available) | the whole suite on the aarch64 engine, as in [the commands below](#linux-aarch64) |

Not tested, and said so in the release notes: musl beyond the wheel smoke test (the only musl
userland would be Alpine, which the project doesn't use), macOS 11 to 14, Intel Macs, i686 (no
wheel is built).

### Linux x86-64

On a 4-thread, 8 GiB container, from the release commit (the CI jobs above are the record; this
reproduces them in one place when CI isn't available, as in a [security release](development.md#security-releases)):

<!-- docs-run: skip="release step 1: an interactive container on a source checkout" -->
```sh
git clone https://github.com/dsd-toolbox/pysacd pysacd-release && cd pysacd-release
podman run --rm -it --memory 8g --memory-swap 8g --cpus 4 --cap-add SYS_PTRACE \
  -v .:/src:ro,Z registry.fedoraproject.org/fedora:44 bash
```

Inside the container:

<!-- docs-run: skip="release step 1: runs as root inside the step 1 container" -->
```sh
dnf -y install shadow-utils util-linux git-core gcc make flac-devel pkgconf-pkg-config findutils binutils diffutils file which python3.13 python3.13-devel clang compiler-rt llvm libasan libubsan liblsan libtsan valgrind cmake libxml2-devel glibc-gconv-extra
useradd -m -d /build ci && cp -a /src /build/pysacd && chown -R ci /build
runuser -l ci
```

As `ci`:

<!-- docs-run: skip="release step 1: the suite on a source checkout inside the step 1 container" -->
```sh
cd ~/pysacd && mkdir -p ~/tmp && export TMPDIR=~/tmp LANG=C.UTF-8
python3.13 -m venv ~/venv && . ~/venv/bin/activate
pip install --require-hashes -r requirements-dev.txt && pip install --no-deps --no-build-isolation -e .
make PORTABLE=1 && make test-tools
ruff check . && mypy src
python3 tools/docs_index.py --check && python3 tools/check_doc_versions.py
PYSACD_TEST_MEMORY_MB=4096 PYSACD_TEST_REPORT=report.json PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest -q tests
python3 -I tools/check_skips.py --job tests report.json
```

*Expected:* every test passes and `check_skips` reports only the skips listed for `tests`.
*Validated:* 2026-11-23 on master after 0.5.5 (364 passed, 25 skipped), with CI's
`compare with sacd_extract` tests too (148 passed, 3 skipped).

### Linux aarch64

<!-- docs-run: skip="release step 1: an interactive aarch64 container on a source checkout" -->
```sh
podman run --rm -it --arch arm64 --memory 8g --cpus 4 -v .:/src:ro,Z registry.fedoraproject.org/fedora:44 bash
```

Then the same commands as for x86-64, without `PORTABLE=1` (`make`). *Expected:* the same counts
as on x86-64. Emulation needs `qemu-user-static` on the host, and the suite takes far longer; it
is not timed. *New:* the suite has never run on aarch64; CI only builds the aarch64 wheel and runs
its smoke test.

## 2. Identity and golden checks

### Against sacd_extract and the previous release, on real discs

`tools/extract_compare.py` runs `pysacd-extract` and `pysacd convert` in all 37 modes with two
source trees, and the `sacd_extract`-compatible modes with `sacd_extract` as a black box (see
[development](development.md#output-through-scarletbook)). The new tree must give the same files,
names and bytes as PREVIOUS in every mode, and match `sacd_extract` wherever PREVIOUS did. Run it on
the release commit before the version bump, so both trees carry PREVIOUS's version.

Build `sacd_extract` from the commit CI pins (`SACD_RIPPER_COMMIT` in
`.github/workflows/ci.yml`):

<!-- docs-run: skip="release step 2: builds sacd_extract from source for the comparison" -->
```sh
git init -q sacd-ripper && cd sacd-ripper
git fetch -q --depth 1 https://github.com/sacd-ripper/sacd-ripper.git a3d981c935c3224217e2842cd492f9351106c81e
git checkout -q FETCH_HEAD
CFLAGS="-std=gnu17 -Wno-error=incompatible-pointer-types -Wno-error=int-conversion -Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" \
  cmake -S tools/sacd_extract -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5
make -C build -j4 && cd ..
```

Build PREVIOUS next to the release tree, then compare:

<!-- docs-run: skip="release step 2: needs real discs, the previous release and the release source" -->
```sh
git -C pysacd-release worktree add ../pysacd-PREVIOUS vPREVIOUS
make -C pysacd-PREVIOUS PORTABLE=1 && make -C pysacd-release PORTABLE=1
cd pysacd-release
python3 tools/extract_compare.py --old ../pysacd-PREVIOUS/src --new src \
  --sacd-extract ../sacd-ripper/build/sacd_extract --no-values --require-sacd-extract \
  DISC1.iso DISC2.iso DISC3.iso DISC4.iso DISC5.iso
```

DISC1 to DISC5 are the maintainer's images of the five discs of the
[minimum set](#5-the-real-disc-corpus). Exit status 0 means no difference between the trees and none
from `sacd_extract` beyond docs/sacd_extract.md. A run that differs between the trees is either the
release's intended change, explained in its changelog section, or a failure.

*Record in the changelog section,* in this form (0.5.5's): "on the same five real discs as for
0.5.3, in all 37 modes (185 runs, 1,386 files). One run differs between the trees: (which mode,
which disc, why). Of `sacd_extract`'s 698 files, 436 are identical and 262 differ only where
docs/sacd_extract.md says so; none differs otherwise."

*Validated:* on 0.5.5's release run (real discs, CHANGELOG 0.5.5); the invocation on 2026-11-23 on
a generated DST disc, PREVIOUS 0.5.5 against master.

### TOC reading on the whole library

The output check reads five discs. The TOC reader sees far more variety (text encodings, odd
timecodes, damaged areas), and a change there reaches beets-pysacd's fingerprints too:

<!-- docs-run: skip="release step 2: needs a library of real discs" -->
```sh
python3 tools/toc_compare.py --old ../pysacd-PREVIOUS/src --new src LIBRARY/*.iso
```

LIBRARY is the folder of the maintainer's SACD image library, read-only. *Expected:* no
difference in any Disc, Area or Track, or in `toc --json`. Last run for 0.4.0 (291 images); new
for every release from 0.5.6.

### PCM goldens

The DSD-to-PCM filter must give the reference vectors' bytes:

<!-- docs-run: skip="release step 2: runs the PCM vectors of a source checkout" -->
```sh
tools/pcm_vectors/run_all.sh /tmp/pcm-vectors
(cd /tmp/pcm-vectors/ref && sha256sum *.i32) | sort -k2 > got.sha256
grep -E '^    [0-9a-f]{64}  ' tools/pcm_vectors/README.md | sed 's/^    //' | sort -k2 > want.sha256
diff want.sha256 got.sha256
```

*Expected:* no output (12 files). The PCM that the shipped engine writes is checked by the FLAC
and WAV modes of the real-disc comparison, byte for byte against PREVIOUS. *Validated:* 2026-11-23
on master after 0.5.5.

## 3. Timed fuzzing

On the release commit, on a lab machine, in the Fedora 44 container of [step 1](#linux-x86-64):

| Target | Parser | Sanitizers | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fuzz_engine` (libFuzzer) | the engine around scarletbook: reader, batches, writers, FLAC, configured runs | ASan, UBSan | 30 min, 2 workers |
| `fuzz_engine` (libFuzzer) | the same | TSan | 10 min |
| `tests/test_fuzz.py` | the PS3 protocol decoder, the PS3 client against a hostile server, the TOC reader on corrupted and truncated images, the `ps3sim` handler | Python | `PYSACD_FUZZ=500000` (about 10 min) |
| `tests/test_safetext.py` | disc and MusicBrainz text | Python | `PYSACD_FUZZ=500000` (about 10 min) |

<!-- docs-run: skip="release step 3: 40 minutes of fuzzing on a source checkout" -->
```sh
make fuzz test-tools
PYTHONPATH=src:tests python3 fuzz/make_seeds.py build/fuzz-seeds
mkdir -p build/fuzz-corpus/engine build/fuzz-tmp
TMPDIR=build/fuzz-tmp build/fuzz_engine -max_len=4194304 -jobs=2 -workers=2 -rss_limit_mb=1500 -timeout=60 \
  -max_total_time=1800 build/fuzz-corpus/engine build/fuzz-seeds/engine fuzz/regressions/fuzz_engine
rm -f build/fuzz_engine && make FUZZ_SAN=thread fuzz
TSAN_OPTIONS=suppressions=tests/tsan.supp TMPDIR=build/fuzz-tmp build/fuzz_engine -max_len=4194304 -timeout=60 \
  -max_total_time=600 build/fuzz-corpus/engine build/fuzz-seeds/engine
PYSACD_FUZZ=500000 PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest -q tests/test_fuzz.py tests/test_safetext.py
```

*Expected:* no crash, sanitizer report or failing seed. A crash's input goes, minimised, into
`fuzz/regressions/fuzz_engine/` with its fix. scarletbook's own parsers are fuzzed in its
repository. *Validated:* 2026-11-23 on master after 0.5.5, 60 s per libFuzzer target and
`PYSACD_FUZZ=5000`.

## 4. Leak and race checks

| Check | Tool | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Memory errors in the suite | ASan, UBSan | CI `tests under ASan + UBSan` |
| Leaks in the engine and scarletbook | LeakSanitizer on every seed, valgrind memcheck on eight | CI `engine leak check`; by hand below |
| Data races between the reader, workers and writer | TSan on the suite, and on the fuzz harness ([step 3](#3-timed-fuzzing)) | CI `tests under TSan` |

<!-- docs-run: skip="release step 4: leak checks on a source checkout" -->
```sh
scripts/leak-check.sh lsan
scripts/leak-check.sh memcheck
```

*Expected:* both exit 0. *Validated:* 2026-11-23 on master after 0.5.5.

## 5. The real-disc corpus

The real discs are the maintainer's SACD image library: images of discs the maintainer owns, read
only and never copied out or named in public. Results are counts, never titles. The minimum set,
the same since 0.5.3 so results compare across releases:

| Disc | Areas | Coding | Layers | Disc text |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | stereo and 5.1 | stereo plain DSD, 5.1 DST | hybrid | yes |
| 2 | stereo and 5.1 | both DST | hybrid | yes |
| 3 | stereo | DST | hybrid | yes |
| 4 | stereo | plain DSD | hybrid | none |
| 5 | stereo | plain DSD | single layer | yes |

**Not in the set yet** (stated as untested until a disc is added): a raw-sector image (2064 or
2448-byte sectors: `pysacd-extract -I` first, since `sacd_extract` refuses them), plain-DSD
multichannel, a multichannel-only disc, Japanese, Chinese or Korean disc text, and discs with
missing frames. The whole library takes part in the [TOC check](#toc-reading-on-the-whole-library).

## 6. Quick start in a fresh container

The README's Quick start, as written, with the wheel from PyPI, in a fresh Fedora 44 container, as a
normal user. The `quickstart` workflow runs it on every pull request with a wheel built from the
branch; this step runs it on what users download. From a clone of the tag:

<!-- docs-run: skip="release step 6: the Quick start of the version being released, in its own container" -->
```sh
git clone --depth 1 --branch vVERSION https://github.com/dsd-toolbox/pysacd pysacd-VERSION
podman run --rm --memory 4g --cpus 2 -v ./pysacd-VERSION:/src:ro,Z registry.fedoraproject.org/fedora:44 bash -euc '
dnf -y -q install python3 python3-pip python3-numpy gcc make shadow-utils util-linux findutils
cp -r /src /qs-src && make -C /qs-src test-tools
useradd -m quickstart && mkdir /work
python3 -I /qs-src/tools/readme_quickstart.py make-disc /work/album.iso
python3 -m pip download --no-deps --only-binary :all: -d /wheel pysacd==VERSION
chown -R quickstart /work
runuser -u quickstart -- python3 -I /qs-src/tools/readme_quickstart.py run --wheel /wheel/*.whl --workdir /work --tracks 3'
```

*Expected:* "README Quick start: 3 steps ran as written; checked 3 'You should see' items". A
release whose `TESTPYPI_PUBLISH` is on can be checked first with `--index-url
https://test.pypi.org/simple/ --extra-index-url https://pypi.org/simple/` on the `pip download`
line. *Validated:* 2026-11-23 with pysacd 0.5.5 from PyPI (its tag predates
`tools/readme_quickstart.py`, so master's copy ran the identical Quick start).

## 7. Docs commands

Every command block in the Markdown carries a docs-run marker: it runs, or it says why it can't
(docs/development.md, [docs commands](development.md#docs-commands-against-a-release)). Two
runs cover them. The `docs-run` workflow runs the marked blocks in a fresh Fedora container
against the release on PyPI, on discs that `tools/docs_fixtures.py` generates; run it from the
Actions tab once the release is on PyPI. Before the tag, run the same blocks, and the Python
blocks, against the release candidate from a source checkout, with `sacd_extract` from
[step 2](#2-identity-and-golden-checks) and Podman so that the blocks skipped for them run too:

<!-- docs-run: skip="release step 7: this check itself, from a source checkout" -->
```sh
python3 -I tools/docs_commands.py list
python3 -I tools/docs_commands.py run --spec pysacd==VERSION --workdir build/docs-commands --sacd-extract ../sacd-ripper/build/sacd_extract --podman
```

*Expected:* `list` reports no block without a marker; `run` reports 0 failed, and every block it
did not run is listed with the reason from its marker. Blocks skipped for a PS3 run against the
release's own `pysacd ps3sim`. *Validated:* 2026-11-24 against 0.5.5 from PyPI: `run` with `--podman`
(21 blocks ran, 0 failed; without `sacd_extract`), and the `docs-run` blocks with Podman (10
passed, 40 skipped with a reason).

## 8. Performance

The by-release table of [performance](performance.md#scarletbook-rs-070): the same rows, machine
and conditions as the last table, PREVIOUS and the two releases before it as columns, VERSION last,
median of 5 runs with the range, and a column "vs PREVIOUS". Conditions: under the machine's
benchmark lock, builds alternated, image in the page cache, output to `/dev/shm`, runs pinned with
`taskset` (`-c 0` for one thread, `-c 0,2,4,6,8` for five), thermal counters read around every run.
Rows:

| Row | Command |
|---|---|
| DST stereo to DSF, 1 thread | `taskset -c 0 pysacd-extract -2 -s --threads 1 -i DISC3.iso` |
| DST stereo to DSF, 5 threads | `taskset -c 0,2,4,6,8 pysacd-extract -2 -s --threads 5 -i DISC3.iso` |
| DST 5.1 to DSF, 5 threads | `taskset -c 0,2,4,6,8 pysacd-extract -m -s --threads 5 -i DISC2.iso` |
| DST 5.1 to DSF, 1 thread, track 1 | `taskset -c 0 pysacd-extract -m -s --threads 1 -t 1 -i DISC2.iso` |
| DST stereo to DSF, 1 thread, an E-core | the first row on an E-core of the same machine |

Record peak memory with each row (`/usr/bin/time -f '%e s %M KB'`): users run pysacd on small NAS
CPUs, so memory and one slow core matter more than the fastest machine.

**Threshold.** A row slower than PREVIOUS with ranges that don't overlap is reported in the
changelog with its cause. A row over 5 % slower, or peak memory over 10 % higher, blocks the tag
until it is explained and accepted in the release issue. *Validated:* on 0.5.5's release run
([scarletbook-rs 0.7.0](performance.md#scarletbook-rs-070)); the E-core row and peak memory are new
from 0.5.6.

## 9. Security

**Before the tag.** The security auditor, a reviewer separate from the release's author, reviews the
range from PREVIOUS's tag to the release commit (`git diff vPREVIOUS HEAD`): parsers, network,
paths, the engine and its FFI, workflows and dependencies. The tag waits for its `go` on that exact
commit; a later commit needs a new `go`. A fix to released code follows
[security releases](development.md#security-releases).

**After publishing.** The files on PyPI are the GitHub release's assets, and each carries a valid
build provenance attestation:

<!-- docs-run: skip="release step 9: checks the files of the version being released, with a signed-in GitHub CLI" -->
```sh
mkdir release-check && cd release-check
gh release download vVERSION -R dsd-toolbox/pysacd -D github
curl -s https://pypi.org/pypi/pysacd/VERSION/json | python3 -I -c 'import json,sys; [print(u["digests"]["sha256"] + "  " + u["filename"]) for u in json.load(sys.stdin)["urls"]]' > pypi.sha256
(cd github && sha256sum -c ../pypi.sha256)
ls github | grep -vc intoto.jsonl && wc -l < pypi.sha256
find github -name '*.whl' -o -name '*.tar.gz' | xargs -I FILE gh attestation verify FILE --repo dsd-toolbox/pysacd
find github -name '*.whl' -o -name '*.tar.gz' | xargs -I FILE gh attestation verify FILE --repo dsd-toolbox/pysacd --bundle FILE.intoto.jsonl
```

*Expected:* every file `OK`, the two counts equal (7 for 0.5.5), every verification passes.
*Validated:* 2026-11-23 on 0.5.5.

**First release from `dsd-toolbox` (0.6.0).** The two verify lines above, with `--repo dsd-toolbox/pysacd`
and without `--bundle`, then with it, have not yet been run on a release signed from that
repository: 0.5.5 and earlier verify only as `aclater/pysacd` and only with `--bundle`
([install](install/README.md#checking-a-download)). Run them on the 0.6.0 files, and if either
fails, correct that section of the install guide before announcing the release. Record which of
the two forms passed here.

## 10. Fresh-eyes review for first releases

For a new minor or major line (0.6.0, 1.0.0) and for a release that adds a component (a new
command, output format or platform), a reviewer who did not write or review the changes, and
gets none of the author's notes, reads the release as a newcomer would. It gets the tag diff from
the previous minor line, the README and `docs/`, and the changelog section, and checks:

- that every changelog claim is true of the diff, and every user-visible change is in the changelog;
- that the docs describe what the code does now, and each new command and option works as written;
- what is untested, or tested only on generated discs, and whether the docs say so;
- API and command-line changes that break callers without a note.

Its findings go in the release issue. Each is fixed or answered before the tag.

## 11. PCM quality comparison

The release's PCM output measured against PREVIOUS's with the pinned suite
([development](development.md#release-quality-comparison)): stereo FLAC and 5.1 WAV at 88.2 and
176.4 kHz, SINAD, THD+N, noise floor, alias rejection and the null depth between the two releases.
On the release commit, in the container of [step 1](#linux-x86-64) with `cargo`, `rust` and
`ffmpeg-free` added, on one lab machine for both versions:

<!-- docs-run: skip="release step 11: builds and measures two releases for about an hour" -->
```sh
python3 tools/quality_compare.py --previous PREVIOUS --candidate . --work ~/tmp/quality --out docs/quality/VERSION.md
```

Add the page to the table in `docs/quality/README.md`, commit both with the release, and link the
page from the release's changelog section, which becomes the release notes. *Expected:* exit status
0 and no figure flagged worse. A figure worse than PREVIOUS's by more than the suite's bound blocks
the tag unless DECISIONS.md in dsd-toolbox/dsd-toolbox explains and accepts it; the page says why.
Unlike the other steps, the version bump doesn't matter here: no figure depends on pysacd's
version string. *Validated:* 2026-11-24 as a trial run, not published, 0.5.5 against the 0.6.0 release
branch with dsd-measure 0.1.1 and an unreleased dsd2pcm; new from 0.6.0.

<!-- docs-audit:begin -->
## After the release: run the docs audit

After the release: run the docs audit. Do it once the tag, the packages and the release notes are public, and before the release is announced.

1. Run the `docs-audit` workflow from the Actions tab of the repository (Run workflow). It runs the docs lint, the link check with external URLs and the docs facts check, and fails if any of them does.
2. Open the checklist it prints: every page that mentions a version, a command-line option or a platform, to compare with the release just published. Fix each mismatch in a docs-only change, or write down why it is right.
3. Record the result in the release notes or the release checklist: the workflow run, and how many checklist items were fixed.

Every project also runs this audit each month (the `docs-monthly` workflow in the DSD Toolbox repository), so a missed audit shows up within a month.
